headline: The classical Lüroth map has one exact periodic point and product multiplier for every finite branch word; primitive necklaces are explicit, while the countable alphabet makes every period countably infinite.
nonclaims: Finite cutoff rows are reproducibility slices; the countable alphabet is the mathematical object and gives countably many points at every positive period.
The weighted source identity and its meromorphic continuation are not a target Euler product, divisor, functional equation, or zero correspondence; A2 and A3 are FAIL.
The absolute primitive-product domain |z|A(Re(s))<1 is distinct from the larger half-plane where 1/(1-zA(s)) is meromorphic away from denominator zeros.
The branch labels and multipliers are not rational primes, prime powers, von Mangoldt weights, or logarithmic lengths.
No arithmetic local datum, root number, automorphy statement, Hilbert-Polya operator, or Route-B input is claimed.

route_a.strongest_failure: the branch alphabet and physical iterate clock have no intrinsic rational-prime carrier; every period has countably infinite points
route_a.strongest_positive: exact countable-branch word/point/multiplier theorem, primitive-necklace ledger, and correctly separated weighted-product and meromorphic domains

theorem.branch_partition: T_L maps each I_m affinely onto (0,1] with derivative a_m=m(m-1); 0 is reached only as the excluded left endpoint limit
theorem.countable_branches: Because the alphabet is countably infinite, every positive period has countably infinitely many coded words and periodic points (with the endpoint convention isolated)
theorem.euler_product_domain: The countable primitive Euler product/log expansion is absolutely convergent only when Re(s)>1/2 and |z| A(Re(s))<1
theorem.full_limit: A(s)=sum_{m=2}^infinity [m(m-1)]^{-s} converges absolutely for Re(s)>1/2 by comparison with sum (m-1)^(-2 Re(s))
theorem.itinerary: The forward itinerary of x_w is w and cyclic rotations describe the same oriented periodic orbit
theorem.meromorphic_extension: Within Re(s)>1/2, 1/(1-z A(s)) is the meromorphic continuation away from denominator zeros; this is broader than the absolute product domain
theorem.primitive_necklaces: Primitive words modulo cyclic rotation are primitive necklaces; finite cutoff q=M-1 has (1/r) sum_{d|r} mu(d) q^{r/d} necklaces of length r
theorem.scope: This is a source-local countable-branch theorem; no target divisor, zero correspondence, or arithmetic prime semantics is asserted
theorem.telescoping_boundary: At s=1, A(1)=sum_{m=2}^infinity(1/(m-1)-1/m)=1, so z=1 is a denominator pole/boundary
theorem.unique_fixed_point: Every finite word has a unique fixed point x_w in its coded cylinder; endpoint ambiguities are confined to the declared countable boundary convention
theorem.weighted_truncation: For finite M, Z_M(z,s)=1/(1-z sum_{m=2}^M [m(m-1)]^{-s}) and its primitive-word product agrees where |z| A_M(Re(s))<1
theorem.word_inverse: For every finite word w, Phi_w=phi_{w_1} compose ... compose phi_{w_r} is affine with contraction product a_{w_j}^{-1}
